articles.title: Digital access to early music
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: What may look to modern readers like a form of secret code in fact opens the door to a fascinating world of historical music: German lute tablature. Developed specifically for the Renaissance lute, this rich notational tradition preserves dances, songs and other musical works that were immensely popular some 500 years ago. As part of an interdisciplinary team of experts, researchers at the University of Bayreuth are now making these sources readable and audible once again through a digital scholarly edition platform.

articles.title: Why molecular cage catalysts show enormous differences in performance
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Chemistry researchers have developed a new way to identify and understand highly effective artificial enzyme-like catalysts using powerful "molecular cages" that mimic the behavior of nature's enzymes. These tiny, hollow molecular structures act like miniature reaction chambers to trap molecules and accelerate chemical reactions. The cages showed enormous differences in performance, with the best catalysts more than 10,000 times more active than the least effective ones.

articles.title: DESTINY model tracks molecular chemistry on uneven, ice-covered grains in interstellar space
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Interstellar space is the scene of active chemical processes: molecules form there in the gas, but also on the surface of tiny dust grains covered in ice. To better represent what happens on these surfaces, astrophysicists at the University of Liège are proposing a deterministic approach based on Markov chains with absorbing states, a mathematical tool that had not yet been utilized in astrochemistry. The paper is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

articles.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
articles.summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile. The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.
